title: Common-cover comparison and ideal detection for ordinary affine descents
statement:
Fix a totally ordered label type $L$. Let $A$ be a rule on reduced finite-type rational schemes admitting a closed embedding in a smooth separated finite-type rational scheme [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data, def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule, def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. It assigns finite ordinary blowup towers with distinct increasing labels, coherent ideals with nonempty nowhere dense regular centers, and regular final scheme; its empty-input tower has length zero. For each open immersion of embeddable inputs over the rational base, its specified label-preserving cartesian contraction comparison deletes exactly the stages whose extended ideals are unit ideals [def-per-ordinary-tower-cartesian-map, def-nagata-extended-ideal, pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-regular-scheme].

Assume padded overlap compatibility as defined in [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data]. Let $S$ be any reduced finite-type rational input and let $B$ be a labeled ordinary tower on $S$ which is an affine descent of $A$, meaning its full pullback to one finite affine-cover coproduct is the assigned tower. Then (i) for every finite affine cover $q:T\to S$ there is an embeddability witness for $T$ and a full labeled cartesian map $A(T)\to B$ over $q$, and for every stage this map detects the global ideal: any ideal $J$ whose pullback is the corresponding center of $A(T)$ equals the center of $B$; (ii) for every other labeled tower $C$ on $S$ which is an affine descent of $A$, there exists a full labeled cartesian map over the identity from $C$ to $B$. The orientation of the map follows the structure $\operatorname{LabeledOrdinaryCartesianMap}(1_S,B,C)$ [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data, def-per-ordinary-tower-cartesian-map]. Neither uniqueness nor cocycle equations are conclusions of this lemma.

proof.text: Now take two finite affine covers $\mathcal U,\mathcal V$ and their combined family. Write $D=A(U\amalg V)$ and let its label list be $\Delta$. The component immersion $U\hookrightarrow U\amalg V$ identifies $A(U)$ with the contraction of $D|_U$, so its labels form a subset of $\Delta$. Suppose $\lambda\in\Delta$ were absent from $A(U)$. Then it is absent from $A(W)$ for every affine open $W\subset U_a\cap V_b$: use the open embedding of $W$ into the $a$th component of $U$ and the hypothesis on $A$. For the other embedding of $W$ into the $b$th component of $U\amalg V$, the same hypothesis says that the $\lambda$ ideal in the full pullback of $D$ is a unit. These $W$ cover every $V_b$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], because $\mathcal U$ covers $S$. Their inverse images cover the corresponding level over $V_b$. The $\lambda$ ideal is already a unit over $U$, since that label was deleted on $U$. It is therefore a unit everywhere on that level of $D$, contradicting its nonempty center. Thus $A(U)$ retains every label of $D$. Interchanging $U$ and $V$ gives the same assertion for $A(V)$. This argument concerns the original label $\lambda$ on the uncontracted tower, so it remains valid across any number of preceding deleted stages. The assumed padded-overlap property supplies the common full local realization, so this argument applies even when the global input is not embeddable.

proof.text:
choose a cover witnessing that B is an affine descent. For any other cover,
form the combined finite family, whose total space is the disjoint union of the two
total spaces. It is again embeddable. The component open immersions compare each
assigned subfamily tower with the contraction of the assigned combined tower.
If a label of the combined tower disappeared on one subfamily, its ideal would be
unit there. On any affine open in an intersection with a chart from the other
subfamily, the two open comparisons contract to the same assigned tower. Padding
restores precisely the missing unit ideals, so the combined ideal is unit on this
affine overlap as well. Such affine overlaps cover every chart of the other family
because the first family covers S. Their inverse images cover each lifted level.
The ideal is therefore unit throughout the combined level, contradicting its
nonempty center. Thus neither covering subfamily loses any label. This argument
uses the original label in the full tower, including across preceding deleted stages.
The padded-overlap comparisons now identify full towers on all chart refinements.
At level zero use the identity on S. Given the comparison at a level, the actual
center ideals agree because equality of sheaf membership is detected on the covering
opens: a section is in the ideal exactly when all its chart restrictions are in it.
The next blowups are identified by their universal property; their pulled-back
ideals are invertible by principalization. Reverse lifts show that the level maps
are isomorphisms, hence cartesian over the identity. Their uniqueness makes the
identifications agree on refinements and permits induction through all labels.
Apply this induction on the lifted chart overlaps of B and A(T). The level maps
glue on their source open covers, and their squares are cartesian locally on the
cover. This gives the required full map on the second cover. Any ideal J having the
prescribed pullback has the same chart restrictions as B's center. The same
sectionwise membership test proves J equals that center; this is DescendsIdeals. For another affine
descent
C, repeat the construction with its witnessing cover to obtain a cartesian map
between B and C over the identity. All labels and the entire center ideals are
preserved. Empty families have zero stages, and empty chart pieces do not change
any sheaf-membership test.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_resolution_descent_comparison {L : Type w} [LinearOrder L]
    (A : OrdinaryZariskiResolutionRule.{u, w} L) (_hpad : A.HasPaddedOverlaps)
    (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (B : LabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme)
    (_hB : A.IsAffineDescent S B) :
    (∀ (T : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (q : T.scheme ⟶ S.scheme),
      ResolutionAffineCover S T q → ∃ hT : T.IsEmbeddable,
        ∃ c : LabeledOrdinaryCartesianMap q B (A.tower T hT), c.DescendsIdeals) ∧
      (∀ C : LabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme, A.IsAffineDescent S C →
        Nonempty (LabeledOrdinaryCartesianMap (𝟙 S.scheme) B C))
